# PV101 Day 7 Daily Run Sheet

Instructor-facing plan for Rich or a substitute | Wednesday, July 15, 2026

Day_07_PV101_Load_Assessment_and_System_Sizing_2026-07-15

Topic: Load Assessment and System Sizing

Class setup: 6 students | 10:00 AM-3:00 PM | Calm, practical, evidence-first instruction

# Teaching frame

Main message: loads drive system sizing, and units make the reasoning inspectable.

Day 7 is guided practice, not a project, proposal, capstone, or presentation.

Use only the documented training values on the worksheet; do not invent equipment or product specifications.

Safety remains part of design: protection, disconnects, labels, and verification points must appear on the one-line diagram.

# Substitute quick start

[ ] Read the full schedule before students arrive.

[ ] Locate emergency disconnects, first-aid supplies, calculator policy, and secure test storage.

[ ] Print student materials and keep answer keys/instructor notes separate.

[ ] Write the day goal, schedule, and stop-work rule on the board.

[ ] If uncertain about equipment or assessment handling, use the reduced-scope path and contact program leadership.

# Learning targets

Calculate daily energy use in watt-hours from a documented loads list.

Use provided assumptions to calculate basic battery Wh/Ah and array watts.

Choose an inverter rating from documented simultaneous AC loads and headroom.

Draw and label a one-line system path with protection, disconnects, and verification points.

Check units, assumptions, and reasonableness before instructor signoff.

# Materials

Chapters 11-12 quiz and key

Day 7 slide deck and whiteboard outline

Student worksheet and guided-practice guide

Calculators, pencils, rulers, scrap paper

Documented RV training loads and provided assumptions

Evidence checklist and reflection sheet

# Daily schedule

| Time | Block | Instructor notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10:00-10:10 | Arrival, attendance, check-in | Students get notebooks and Chapters 11-12 quiz. Instructor displays: Measure. Verify. Document. Then proceed. |
| 10:10-10:20 | Safety reset + day goal | Review stop-work authority and explain that today is guided sizing practice, not a project or product proposal. |
| 10:20-10:35 | Morning quiz | Individual Chapters 11-12 reading check. Ten questions; quiet work. |
| 10:35-10:55 | Quiz correction | Correct together in a different color. Review current-source verification, AHJ/permitting roles, units, and safest-answer thinking. |
| 10:55-11:20 | Whiteboard review | Connect Chapters 1-12: loads drive sizing; safety and verification constrain every decision. |
| 11:20-11:30 | Break | Reset attention. Calculators, worksheets, and pencils staged after break. |
| 11:30-12:00 | Slides + worked example | Model watts x hours, total Wh/day, battery Wh/Ah, array watts, and inverter headroom using the provided training values. |
| 12:00-12:30 | Guided example check | Students complete one example with instructor pauses after each calculation. Check units before accepting answers. |
| 12:30-1:00 | Lunch | Worksheets remain on tables. No kit wiring or energized work. |
| 1:00-1:15 | Practice introduction | Explain the RV training load worksheet, required assumptions, evidence boxes, and instructor checkpoints. |
| 1:15-1:50 | Guided worksheet: loads + battery | Students calculate daily Wh and basic storage. Instructor checks totals before array sizing. |
| 1:50-2:15 | Guided worksheet: array + inverter | Students calculate array watts and identify concurrent AC load plus headroom. |
| 2:15-2:30 | Diagram + protection points | Students draw a one-line system path and mark conceptual protection, disconnects, labels, and meter points. |
| 2:30-2:45 | Verification + revision | Peer checks math, units, assumptions, and diagram. Instructor signs only after corrections. |
| 2:45-2:55 | Reflection + evidence upload | Complete reflection and upload/submit the worksheet as directed. |
| 2:55-3:00 | Cleanup + dismissal | Calculators returned, papers collected, tables clear, next-day final reminder given. |

# Safety and instructional stop conditions

A student uses an assumption or specification not provided in the worksheet.

Units are missing or mixed without conversion.

A sizing answer is copied without work or cannot be explained.

The diagram omits protection, disconnects, or return paths.

Discussion drifts into physical wiring; this day is paper/calculator practice.

# Reduced-scope backup

Day 7: if calculators or printing fail, complete one class example on the whiteboard and have students show units and reasonableness on notebook paper. Day 8: if final-test printing fails, run structured review and reflection; do not improvise a different final from memory. Reschedule the secured assessment.

# Early finishers

Day 7: check every unit, redo one calculation independently, and write one sentence explaining each sizing result. Day 8: quietly review answers, then begin the reflection only after turning in the final.
